rows.title: A trivial Bash call waited on the full work of the heavy Bash hooks
rows.note: Each fix (48bfc77, d36db7b, 3a3b8128, this one) cut the same shape in other hooks: a hook doing its full work on a call it has nothing to do with; the doctor's hook_full_work rule is the detector for the next one. 2026-10-05 (load 330-410), CPU on a plain call in a scratch HOME: commit-report (the after setter) sourced review-journal on every call, 80 ms; worker-launch-gate started 14 processes before its own prefilter, 76 ms; pr-ready-mattermost ran 3 jq and the library, 57 ms. commit-report and pr-ready-mattermost now leave before the library when the command with line continuations, quotes and backslashes dropped names no git / gh; worker-launch-gate after one jq, its prefilter words read with [[ =~ ]]; each 15-18 ms against 8-10 for a bare bash. comment-gate's raw *git* check missed `g'i't commit`, which rj_segments unquotes; it reads the flattened command now. Red on the old hooks: test_worker_launch_gate_visibility (llm-legs), test_commit_report, test_pr_mattermost, test_comment_gate (claude-setup). Before setter left: review-owner-gate (review-bench, 44 ms: 2 jq and review-journal on every Bash call), handed off in docs/handoffs/2026-10-04-hook-floors.md.

rows.title: context-nudge read a 1 MiB transcript tail through jq on every tool call
rows.note: Design §4: 79 ms a call before the 64 KiB tail read, 62 ms after; its own tail read cut it, not the fast path.

rows.title: An Edit or Write waits over 500 ms on hooks: edit-conflict-notice before, commit-journal after
rows.note: 2026-10-07: 344 ms p50 (watch, 128 calls in 1 h; 427 ms over 24 h). Setters measured per hook on the joined batches: after, instruction-watch check 196 ms p50 (203 ms CPU), set the after side on 123 of 127 calls; before, edit-conflict-notice 116 ms (76 CPU), instruction-bloat-gate 75, worker-pin-gate write 46. Cause of the after side: Claude Code's Edit and Write rename a new file over the old one (new inode), which moves the directory's mtime, and instruction_visible_cached stamped every repository directory, so every Edit rebuilt the whole git enumeration (~240 ms vs a 20 ms hit). Fixed: a moved repository directory is revalidated by a one-level listing (_instruction_moved_dirs_kept; test_a_file_replaced_in_place_reuses_the_enumeration, red on the old code); bench at load 50: check after an edit 308-514 ms old, 191-348 new. Expected after landing: the after side drops to statusline-workdir-hook (~70 ms), the floor to ~200 ms, still over the 150 ms note; the next setter is edit-conflict-notice before (git status of the edited path per call, its purpose), held as hook-sync-edit-conflict-notice / hook-p50-edit-conflict-notice by the hooks area, so this run left it. Ruled out: commit-journal (no longer an Edit hook). Per-side dispatcher stays Egor's declined trade (2026-10-05).

rows.title: A non-trivial Bash call waits over 500 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-06 03:29 launch, load 100-150: 370 ms (watch); setters moved to instruction-write-gate before and instruction-watch check after (138 and 77 ms CPU mean, the two dearest per-call hooks; neither held by harness-hooks-20261006T032924Z-3077). Cut, CPU p50 over 21-30 paired runs on a copy of the live watch state: check 119 to 92 ms, gate 35 to 25. The check's load_baseline read its ~55 KB stat join from a here-string, which bash 5.3 writes through a forked child past the pipe size (14 ms CPU, ~55 ms wall per quiet call); now one IFS split. Both hooks read the payload with jq straight off stdin (no cat), resolve their directory by expansion (no dirname pair), and skip mkdir when the state dir exists. Test: test_instruction_watch_perf quiet check runs no cat, dirname or mkdir and no byte-wise read (red on the old code). Checked, not worth it: storing the visible cache's paths bare (0.6 ms CPU; the 22 ms first seen was load). Left: about 10 process starts per quiet check (jq, git rev-parse, readlink, 3 awk, 2 stat, rm, touch). Closed as handoff, not fixed: the close rerun read the unlanded fix regressed at 784-804 ms, load 150-166 (handoff item 3). 2026-10-05 14:06 doctor run, load 330-410: 2077 ms; review-flow-gate (hook-sync-review-flow-gate) and commit-journal (hook-p50-commit-journal) are rows of the hooks run harness-hooks-20261005T061324Z-2ae0, so harness-hook-waits-20261005T061316Z-5d3a left them and cut what a plain call paid elsewhere, about 125 ms CPU: worker-launch-gate 76 to 18 ms, commit-report 80 to 15, pr-ready-mattermost 57 to 15 (floor-trivial-bash-readonly-fastpath). Still full work on every Bash call: review-owner-gate (review-bench, handoff), report-flush (46 ms on every tool call, report-bus started with nothing pending; a builtin pending glob over ~/.cache/claude-reports/*/pending is 17 ms of builtins). Found, not this area's: claude-setup tests/test_review_journal.sh fails at load ~430 on base and branch alike in its anonymous concurrent snapshot block (:135-167). With both bash:other setters removed the 10-03 floor still read 467-1010 ms at CPU busy 0.9-1.0: the per-call fan-out of 18 PreToolUse and 10 PostToolUse processes. Dispatcher per side is Egor's trade (handoff). Setters: review-flow-gate before, commit-journal after (both claude-setup); their shared cost is the content snapshot pair (rj_snapshot_repos ~130 of 412 traced ms). 2026-10-04: mean 2657 ms over 8986 calls on 10-03 (3774 on 10-04 under load average ~200); removing commit-journal saves 1081 ms, review-flow-gate 386, commit-report 64, everything else under 15. Both setters (and worker-launch-gate, instruction-watch check next) are problems of harness-hooks-20261004T013933Z-5514, as on 09-30, 10-01 and 10-03, so this run changed none of them; it cut the forks of the hooks no run holds (comment-gate exits before review-journal on a call naming no git; worker-* exit on a main-session call). 2026-10-03: paired p50 467-1010 ms with both setters removed, CPU busy 0.9-1.0 in 20 of 22 hours: the 18-hook bash fan-out per side is structural. Ruled out: the 4ca8de1 session-repo fan-out (381 vs 459 ms at 5+ repos, most calls in 1-2), vendor replacement of attribution snapshots (none found), a fixer limit change. See the handoff. 2026-10-06 night 20261006T032009Z-f253 (handoff 2026-10-04-hook-floors): review-owner-gate exits on builtins when the command names no review-bench (84 to 15 ms wall on a plain call) and report-flush when the payload session's and _orphan's queues hold nothing (69 to 9 ms), both under bash 3.2.

rows.title: test_worker_run · llm-legs 24 h cost exceeds 2 h limit due to frequent runs and concurrent load
rows.note: 2026-10-09 (4 h 01 min over 170 runs): the slowest parts are wait-bound, not CPU-bound (fastest-quintile wall/CPU s: watchdog 125/16, files 63/22, attribution 58/24), so shards cut their wall even on a loaded machine: watchdog 4 shards, files 3, attribution 2; sharded and whole runs give the same asserts (files 63+69+116, attribution 66+258). Direct runs now shard too (tests/lib/suite-journal.sh). Left: watchdog's paused and frozen cases flake at load 250+ sharded or whole (the stub's 1-3 s turns race the watchdog's first transcript read), and the pool/vendor_files parts (82/41, 80/41) stay whole. 2026-10-07: the 17 h 22 min red was the statusline probe journaling one live 27-minute run-suites run 22 times, each row carrying the suite times so far; the probe now skips a suites run whose pid ps still lists while its progress file stands, and load_tests collapses such snapshots. The Tests rules had read only test-history since e5bd8fd1 (the probe skips runs with a run-suites journal row), so they missed nearly every real run; load_tests now reads ~/.cache/run-suites/runs.jsonl too. The true 24 h family cost is ~66 000 s: ~30 family runs a day (worker named runs 42 %, chat named runs of all 18 parts 29 %, full runs 10 %), each part's wall 4-6x its quiet minimum under load (quiet sum 884 s, CPU ~615 s). Cut: test_worker_run_claims held a 40 s stub sleep it then waited out (~37 s a run), now the gate. Ruled out: no fixed latency in worker-run's supervisor (run_with_deadline returns on the child's exit; a cycle is ~3400 traced lines of small forks); the watchdog suite's waits are its idle and deadline windows themselves. 2026-10-08: cost_line now charges a split family's run for its slowest part (the wall one agent waits); the parts' summed machine time over 2 h stays a watch.

rows.title: Background work that never ends held every end-of-turn ask for hours: a Storybook server, a night-job Monitor, agents launched one after another (35 h in one chat)
rows.note: 2026-10-29: the regression since 10-26 is cache-keepalive.py (claude-setup@745c775e, 10-25). Its asyncRewake pings wake an idle chat every 58 min while a background task runs, and each ping's stop arrives with stop_hook_active true. stop-dispatch.sh ran its hold clock only at stop_hook_active false, so an overdue hold waited out every ping for the next real stop. 77a2b895: hold from 22:03:40Z, pings 23:01:34/23:59:35/00:57:36Z all skipped-busy, cap ran the asks only at 01:12:13Z (hits.jsonl observed 11312 s), streak 10436 s. ac22ec9e 20:18:45-22:35:08Z and 2ddedf36 run through the same ping stops (keepalive journal ping ts = stop ts - 4 s). The clock is never touched at an active stop, which is how elimination proves the flag. Fix: an overdue hold runs its asks at a re-entry too (it clears active). Every ask since the hold began was skipped, so none blocked the turn being continued. The only other blocker, worker-run-backstop, bounds its own repeats. The re-entry after those asks starts a fresh hold and asks nothing. Test: test_stop_dispatch 'an overdue hold kept its asks from a re-entry' (red on the old code by a fixture replay, old vs new dispatcher). With pings every 58 min and the cap at 3600 s, a streak now ends at the first stop past the cap, so it stays under 2 h. Accepted: a ping turn whose overdue asks block becomes a work turn, not an 'ok', and resets the keepalive's ping count. Ruled out: pid change (one pid per chat throughout), other sessions in the process (none), deleted held files (since kept, per hits.jsonl). 2026-10-07 review: both 2026-10-06 evidences are the same closed-chat streak, the dispatcher kept its cap. 2ddedf36: cap ran the asks 06:41:53Z (pid 24067), skipped stops to 07:37:38Z, resumed as pid 8381 at 10:23:37Z, skipped to 11:10:23Z (16011 s streak, 47 min of the new process). 40991e51: 06:37:00Z pid 96678, resumed pid 33575 10:31:52Z, cap ran the asks 11:39:29Z (17454 s streak). Pids from the folded hook-time rows (stop-dispatch.sh ppid column). stop-dispatch.sh holds asks for background work at most STOP_DISPATCH_HELD_CAP (3600 s), then runs them at that stop with busy empty and the journal line's held naming what it would have called busy, and the hold restarts; ask-span-drill stays silent under STOP_HELD; ask-run-unfinished also sees waiter tasks under the 2.1.285 label subagent. The doctor's ask-busy rule does not see asks run under held, by design. The 2026-09-30 06:55-08:16 regression was transitional (tasks started before e5909cd landed). The 2026-10-01 regression (10896605, 10:17-13:08Z, 10269 s) was the 959efae stale-hold rule misfiring: no stop from 10:32 to 12:11Z because a task notification at 11:40Z opened a 31-min turn, the old tasks ended inside it and a new one started, so 'no stop for the cap and none of its tasks live' restarted the hold of a live chat. The held file is now 'since chat-pid' ($PPID, the Claude Code process: hook-time rows show one stable ppid per chat process) and only a different process (a closed chat resumed) restarts it; old-format files restart once. Ruled out: notice timing, ask-span-drill, worker-run holds (busy was bg-task throughout). Risk to watch: a harness that wrapped hooks in a per-call shell would restart every hold and bring the unbounded hold back; this rule would show it. The 2026-10-06 regression (2ddedf36, 28600 s) is the doctor's streak crossing a closed chat: held asks ran 17:52:24Z, the old process's last stop was 17:53:39Z, `claude --resume` (pid 24067) started 01:32:12Z and the cap ran the asks 03:30:55Z, so the asks waited 1 min + 1 h 56 min of live process. The dispatcher kept its spec; the doctor now ends a streak where a stop line's pid repeats after a change (a chat process; a pid new on every stop, a per-call shell, still streaks), which needs stop-dispatch.sh to journal pid (its chat_pid) on each line: that half is in claude-setup, so the fix stays pending until both files are committed.

rows.title: A chat start waits over 1000 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-09 fixed: the setter was instruction-watch baseline, 609 ms p50 over 303 starts in 48 h (486 ms CPU), 1 483 ms p50 in the night launch hour at load 280. Its stdout is empty unless INSTRUCTION_WATCH_CHAT=all (a between-sessions check never reverts), so the hook now forks the baseline behind `pending-<session>` (the pid) and returns: 129 ms against 2 547 ms on a copied state dir at load 260, byte-identical baseline. Every writing call waits for it first (instruction_baseline_wait in instruction_inflight_mark and in check, 8 s cap, a dead pid or the cap drops the marker; the background run journals as `instruction-watch.sh baseline-bg`). Test: test_instruction_gate_tripwire (detached start, the first gate call waits, a dead writer's marker), red on the old hook and with the gate's wait removed. Narrowed: a write by a process outside this session landing while its baseline runs (~0.1-3 s after start) is in that baseline; every other live session's check still reports it. Left on the start: statusline-workdir-hook (26 ms p50) and the branch-slug one-liner. Not done: settings.json `async` (needs Egor, speed design §5 Never).

rows.title: A turn end waits over 1000 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-10-10 (night 4c4e): two asks of the chain are gone, the reading-line ask (Egor, claude-setup@4c7eaf02) and ask-run-unfinished's live-run walk (tonight). Last hour p50 105 ms, under the 150 ms note; the 24 h p50 of 281 ms still carries the hours before. Proof: the 24 h p50 under the note. 2026-10-09 cut, kept open: 335 ms p50 in 1 h (stop-dispatch 347 ms CPU avg; notices word-journal 60, chat-names 52, word-attested 19, reports 10; asks run-unfinished 44, word-reading 24, span-drill 12, mattermost 10). At load 280 a stop is ~30 process starts at 50-150 ms each, so forks are the lever: 11 cut a quiet stop (worker-run-backstop: cat, date, the progress cat|jq|awk unless a progress file names the session, rm of an absent hold; stop-dispatch: dirname x2, the timeout subshell, own mktemp and rm), tests test_worker_run_backstop and claude-setup test_stop_dispatch count them, red on the old code. Cheapest cut left: run the backstop in prerun beside the notices, saves ~30 ms x 400/day = 12 s/day, costs an ordering guard (its words_sync races the notices' store reads, stop-dispatch prerun comment). Below the 150 ms note only a one-process stop.d, the dispatcher class Egor declined 2026-10-05; handoff proposes the dismissal. 2026-10-01 ruled out: blanket parallel asks (breaks notice-before-ask order), a vendor replacement for the busy/held journal contract.

rows.title: instruction-watch baseline watched ~/.claude trees nothing loads, and every baseline carried them forward
rows.note: Owner decision 2026-10-04 (Harness Doctor): cut, limit stays; the cut is the one of this hook's hook_sync / hook_every_call row. Wall over 1 s at CPU 0.3-0.45 s is load; a hook_p50 judged per load band or on CPU is proposed to the doctor's owner. 2026-10-04 at load 220-230 on 10 cores (logo-vectorizer-bench batch plus the night): regressed to 2.8 s wall p50 at 442 ms CPU (25 runs, 4 h); the cut watch set holds, the excess is load. Reopened, narrowed to load; a load-banded hook_p50 is proposed in the handoff. 285 of 468 watched rows sat under ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces (catalog clones the harness auto-update pulls; installed plugins load from plugins/cache), plugins/.trash and a hidden top-level backup. Pruning the walk alone changed nothing: the between-sessions check pins every row of the newest baseline, so the set only grew. Now the walk prunes them and every baseline row and visible path under them is dropped (INSTRUCTION_HOME_UNLOADED_ERE). A/B on a copy of the live state, alternating runs: baseline 3.1 s to 1.46 s at load ~140, 5.0 s to 2.6 s at load ~330; quiet check 1.13 s to 0.94 s at load ~330. Also ends the false CHANGED reports on marketplace README pulls (21 log lines). Ruled out: the walk itself (17-25 ms), the reverts/ directory (maxdepth 1 never descends it). Test: tests/test_instruction_watch_perf.py three unloaded-tree cases. 2026-10-05: re-fixed at the shared cause, the enumeration every baseline and check repeats. It is cached on its inputs' stamps (hook-every-call-instruction-watch).

rows.title: worker-launch-gate over 150 ms a run
rows.note: 2026-10-04: cut: after its variable expansion the gate greps once for every later check's literal (prefix dropped, so a superset) and leaves when none is there: a plain write call 230 to 76 ms CPU, 1.2 to 0.36 s wall at load 220; 258 adversarial old/new verdict pairs identical (220 denies). Test: test_worker_launch_gate_visibility.sh, two jq starts on a plain call (four before). Narrowed to its process count: about 60 starts on a plain non-read-only Bash call (30 grep, 7 tr, 6 sed, 5 head, 5 awk, 4 jq, 2 realpath), most of them the owned-class checks run unconditionally; command length adds 10-20 % (13 KB heredoc vs 39 bytes). Not cut in a night run: it is a deny gate, and the cut (one jq, one grep -Eq over every owned regex before the per-class greps, wait_default read only for relay polls) needs its adversarial pass. Proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: logo-vectorizer-bench over 13 400 loose git objects
rows.note: Writers: unreachable hash-object -w blobs of untracked bench outputs from llm-legs worker-run snapshots (14 620 of the 15 975 loose objects written 07-10 local on 10-03 are shas in dirty-before/after-shas of the 213 runs with workdir logo-vectorizer-bench since 10-01 22:00; the 10-02 fixer's 'no worker run since 09-30' was wrong) and claude-setup review-journal rj_hash_paths (the 10-02 burst). git gc --auto does not fix it: it only repacks reachable objects and leaves unreachable ones younger than gc.pruneExpire loose with a 'too many unreachable loose objects' warning, which under autoDetach becomes a gc.log that blocks auto gc for a day (git 2.49, reproduced in a scratch repo). Fix: worker-run pack_loose_objects runs the maintenance loose-objects task (threshold gc.auto, default 6 700) plus prune-packed after every after-snapshot, which packs any loose object of the repository, review-journal blobs included; tested in test_worker_run_files snapshot_blobs_packed_tests. Left: review-journal still never packs in a repository with chats and no worker runs (handoff); in a repository with no commits the loose-* packs are only consolidated by a manual gc (gc.autoPackLimit needs a commit or fetch to fire). Ruled out: gc.log, gc.auto=0, stashes, worktrees, night-run base snapshots.

rows.title: stop-dispatch ran its hooks one after another and forked per worker-run record
rows.note: The dispatcher's critical path was serial: the backstop, then the notices, then every ask one after another, and three of them (dispatcher, backstop, ask-run-unfinished) forked tr per unfinished worker-run record (22 of 732 tonight) to read its launcher; plus a jq per journal record and four for the payload. Now the launcher is read with a builtin, the backstop runs beside the notices, the asks run at once after them, and one jq builds the journal line. A/B at load 50-60 on the real run root: 1.24 s to 0.34 s on a small transcript. Ruled out as the dispatcher's own: Python start of the notices (~70-140 ms each, parallel).

With the hook-sync-stop-dispatch cuts, 31 MB with a notice ~2.0 s to ~0.9 s. rows.title: test_llm_limits · llm-legs costs ~3 h of wall clock a day: one ~375 s serial suite run 27 times
rows.note: 2026-10-03: the 375 s serial monolith was split into tests/test_llm_limits{,_claudeb,_refresh,_render,_grok}.sh over tests/llm_limits_harness.sh, proven call-for-call equivalent; daily machine time stayed the same because the doctor sums a family's parts. Regressed 2026-10-07 at 11293 s / 77 runs: the parts ran ~30 s each at low load except _render at ~131 s, whose 10 prov/exp collections ran with the real HOME and each made a live ElevenLabs balance request (llm-limits.sh share/elevenlabs_balance.py, ~9.5 s at 7% CPU; ~770 live API calls a day). 2026-10-08 fix: the harness exports ELEVENLABS_KEYS to a missing fixture file (also shields the real key mirrors the elevenlabs-one-pool branch syncs on every writing poll), those calls get an empty fixture HOME, and three sleep-1 birth-order loops became born_in_order (touch -t backdates the birth time); side by side at load ~5 the render part went 135 s -> 33 s, the family's summed run ~257 s -> ~160 s. Ruled out: no other part calls the collector with the real HOME (a wrapper logged every call); the remaining cost is ~400 collector calls at ~0.1-0.3 s CPU with no hot spot; the sleeps left (render 35/61 rollout mtime vs cache mtime, claudeb sleep 2 under a 1 s timeout, grok lockf 5 s holder killed at once) are load-bearing or free. 34 of 77 runs were _grok alone named by workers (tests/affected), not a repeat loop. rows.title: The run backstop held a chat whose Fable worker had delegated its brief to nested Opus runs

fixes.by: Updater doctor chat (llm-legs@c9087e4b), recorded by night fixer harness-stop-hooks-20261006T234309Z-703e

rows.note: 2026-10-30 ruled out (night fixer harness-stop-hooks-20261030T052121Z-3ae0): the new event, 02:52:44Z/1db76c56 (system fixer run system-system-20261030T023135Z-005c, CLAUDEB_WORKER=1), is the headless branch of 1375fd54, not a chat run: its last answer left a background test-harness shell live (a PATH grep shim calling itself), the hold asked once, the worker TaskStop'd it and restated its answer at 02:53:05Z, 21 s, where claude -p would have held the run to the shell's timeout. Hook reached its goal; stop-dispatch.sh records every backstop block as `held`, so the doctor's fact reads "held a run no wait owns" for this ask too (label only, same row; not split, a separate ident would only re-open the same correct-by-spec verdict). The 00:50:09Z/ac22ec9e event is the one ruled out below. 2026-10-30 ruled out again (night fixer harness-stop-hooks-20261030T023055Z-1825), the same chat and spelling: 2026-10-30 00:50:09Z/ac22ec9e held claudeb-1793321161-3268-0721 (pixel-forge pick judge). Launch: `(worker-run run claudeb --brief brief-opus.md > run-opus.log 2>&1 &); worker-run run codex ... > run-sol.log` in one background Bash, so the Opus run's starter file is empty and its exec'd wait reparented out of the tree; the Bash ended with the Sol run at 00:49:32Z. The only waiter was then a background `until grep -q '^STATUS' run-opus.log; do sleep 20; done` (the accepted poll miss). The chat ran `worker-run wait <id> --report` 4 s after the hold, and that run ended 00:52Z. 2026-10-29 ruled out (night fixer harness-stop-hooks-20261029T053345Z-3c5c): the hold of 2026-10-28 07:20:26Z/ac22ec9e (pixel-forge judges) was right by spec. One background Bash ran `(worker-run run claudeb|codex --brief … > log 2>&1 &)` four times and ended in 1 s. Each run_run's start_run read $PPID, the detached subshell already gone, so all four starter files are empty. Its exec'd `worker-run wait` was reparented to launchd, outside the chat's tree, so it would wake no one. The chat's only waiter was a background `until [ $(grep -l ^EXIT: j5-*.log | wc -l) -ge 4 ]; do sleep 30; done`, the poll the note below accepts as a miss. The hold moved the chat to `worker-run wait <id> --report` x4 in one background Bash within 6 s. The house launch is `worker-run run … as ONE background Bash` (worker-launch-gate DIRECT_ASK). Considered and declined: owning runs by the Stop payload's running background_tasks (the dispatcher's held bg-task:1 at that stop was the poll). It ends all spelling chases, but a server or Monitor would own every run for its life, losing the boundedness this row chose. 2026-10-19 fifth spelling, 21:56:16Z and 21:56:47Z/b22790bc (arbostar-logo): a background Bash ran stage.sh -> launchm.sh, whose `id=$(worker-run start ... | grep -o ... | head -1)` made the recorded starter ($PPID) the pipeline subshell, dead at once (starter pid = run pid - 1), while stage.sh then waited in turn (collect.sh); the stops fell before or between its waits. worker-run start now records the chain from its parent up to the chat's claude (share/processes.sh starter_chain; parent alone when no claude is above, as codex/gemini workers), and the backstop owns a run while any link lives: the script, or the background Bash whose end wakes the chat. Test: test_worker_run_backstop.sh, a dead first link with a live second (block on the old code) and starter_chain on a fake ps. Accepted: a background Bash that starts runs and then never ends (a server) owns them for its life. Shared cause of all four fixes: owned() matched one spelling of owner at a time (relay tags, scripts waiting in turn, literal ids in a background loop), and each new spelling read as no owner. Fourth cause, the four holds of 2026-10-09/10 (bca23aef 12:08Z, c0f23f02 19:04Z, 233cceb1 23:13Z and 02:13Z), every chat with its background wait live: ids read from a file (`for r in $(cat runs.txt)`, `while read m r ... < runs-r2.txt`, `cut -f2 runs.tsv | while read id`) and the verb behind a variable (`RB=.../review-bench; $RB wait A; $RB wait B`, B held while A's wait ran). Fixed by deleting id matching: any live `worker-run wait` / `review-bench wait` command line under the chat owns all its runs and reviews, since its end wakes the chat and the next stop checks again; worker-run wait is bounded, so no wait silences the hold for good. Accepted miss: a run whose sibling has a wait and it has none is held only at the sibling's wake. Still held: polling loops with no wait verb (`until [ -e panel.exit ]; do sleep 20; done`). The --unowned mode went with it: claude-setup@62caa56 dropped its only caller. Earlier: literal `worker-run wait <id>` loops (19e9f508), log-audit chunk runs (c9087e4b), nested Opus runs (f72bf339).

rows.title: worker-spawn-hook slower in chats with 5+ repositories

rows.title: worker-run ends its own caffeinate and the shell forked around it as run orphans; nohup'd jobs of builder workers and the on-purpose detaches stay fixed
rows.note: 2026-10-29 (night 74c1): the 49 of 2026-10-29 are one logo-vectorizer-bench claudeb builder run (claudeb-1793283123-73926-2978, reason done, 91 min): its two nohup'd `batch.py` slot batches (pids 52425, 52435, 103 profile jobs, queued 78 min behind other lanes' traces) and the champ98 job tree (p01a) its first slot had run for 19 min, which its result left "running for the resume chunk" with a `kill -TERM` line; end_run_orphans ended them as designed, so the resume plan's results never came. Five more self-ended bench runs since 2026-10-23 promised work still running or in the background (ux3 7, arbostar-logo 1, logo-vectorizer-bench 65, 8, 6, 10): no brief told a worker its jobs end with the run. BRIEF_PREAMBLE's WAITING clause now says a job still running at return is killed with the run, so the worker stops it and puts its command in the resume plan; the proof is fewer orphans of self-ended runs. Ruled out: run_env_holders catching another session's traces (every ended pid descends from the run's own batch.py); a watchdog cut (exit 0, no `killed`). 2026-10-14 (night 8004): the 14 of 2026-10-14 are one logo-vectorizer-bench codex builder run (codex-1791930719-67752-2ffd, its nohup'd a7-children chain53-55 tracer jobs) the idle watchdog cut at 05:03 (`killed`: idle 1800). Codex exits 0 on TERM with no final answer, and worker-run read `killed` on exit 143/137 only, so the run was journaled reason done and the rule counted the jobs cut with it as left behind; 6 codex runs since 2026-10-11 were watchdog kills (idle 3, deadline 1, term 2) journaled done. The watchdog now writes `killed` only over a live child, the race the exit-code check guarded, and the journal and the KILLED: line read it whatever the exit code (test_worker_run_watchdog wd-idle-exit0, both asserts red on the old code). The caffeinate pairs held: none after the last run launched before llm-legs@1c394a26 (17:41Z). Found, not fixed: `instruction-watch.sh baseline` (claude-setup, a sync SessionStart hook, timeout 60) still running when a short claudeb run ended, 7 in 4 runs since 2026-10-10: the CLI exited without waiting for it; the hook's own >9 s is the hook-cost area's. 2026-10-13 (night 3131): the 90 of 2026-10-12/13 (351 by 14:41) are two per run of nearly every run since 05dbad63 (2026-10-08) landed: `bash -c # Double-forked…` plus `caffeinate -i -w <supervisor>`. The supervisor's `(cd / && env -u WORKER_RUN_ID caffeinate … &)` forks a shell to run the `cd / &&` list, that shell keeps WORKER_RUN_ID and waits as caffeinate's parent, so run_env_holders takes it and caffeinate (an Apple binary, no env shown) as its descendant; an `exec` drops the shell. The old harness stub caffeinate exited at once, so test_worker_run_lifecycle never saw it; the stub now lives until its -w pid ends and lines 45 and 427 are red on the old code. The other detaches (llm-reset-redeem, pack, instruction pump, session-trash) are simple commands, already exec'd, and never appeared. Beyond those pairs: logo-vectorizer-bench builders' nohup'd python/inkvec jobs (codex-1791889626, failed, 16) and night fixers' own run-suites trees in a few self-ended runs, the nohup family the rule counts as designed. Earlier: 2026-10-10 (night 4c4e): the instruction tripwire's detached `hs -c … m.pump()` poke (1 orphan of a self-ended failed run, 06:39) drops WORKER_RUN_ID like session-trash's purge (test_instruction_gate_tripwire); 28 run-suites orphans of 2026-10-09 08:48 were a done review fixer's own nohup'd run-all past the Bash cap, the nohup family; chrome-native-host orphans of 2026-10-07 never recurred. A run the watchdog cut (runs.jsonl reason wall, idle, deadline, silent, term or signal) ends its detached jobs with it, so worker_orphans_line counts only the orphans of runs that ended on their own; test_wait_journal's deadline row is red on the old code. Both fixes hold: of 45 orphans 2026-10-07 14:00 to 2026-10-09 03:38, none is session-trash's purge or worker-run's pack. rows.title: context-nudge did its full work on a trivial Bash call
rows.note: PostToolUse on every tool: jq on the payload, wc, tail|grep for a boundary and tail|jq for the size, whatever the context. Its work is per call by design, so the cut is a ceiling: lib/context-size.jq with `--arg bound 1` also prints the counted usage's output_tokens plus the bytes of its line and every later one; the hook keeps size+that, the transcript size and path in <session>.size, and while no nudge is spent and ceiling + bytes written since + 20000 (CONTEXT_NUDGE_SKIP_MARGIN: reminders and tool schemas Claude Code adds unwritten) stays under stage1 it exits after wc (2 forks instead of 6). A token is at least a byte, so the skip never hides a crossing the transcript shows. Test: test_context_nudge.sh (no tail under the ceiling, red on old; growth that can reach stage1 is read again and nudges). Ruled out: dropping the payload jq (top-level key order is the only other reader) and a time-based throttle (no bound on growth).

rows.note: 2026-10-29 (run harness-speed-delegation-reviews-20261029T112106Z-79cf): ruled out again after 8b0a06e7, which removed the one non-model hold (slot room); what is left of the 1.94 OM/d is reviewer model time, which Speed never trades, plus the 2 s panel poll in review-bench share/rbench/cli.py wait_panel (PANEL_POLL_S, one `ps` per poll, ~1 s a review x ~3 a day = ~3 s/day). Cheapest cut: poll a cheap file (panel.handoff) every 0.25 s and `ps` every 2 s saves ~900 ms x 3/day = 2.7 s/day, costs a 6-line loop in review-bench and an exit moment still read after clone cleanup (the handoff is written before _close_panel_clones, so waiting on the file alone would not be output-equivalent); a bare PANEL_POLL_S 0.5 saves 0.75 s a review for 4x the `ps` spawns (1440 vs 360 over a 12 min wait), a CPU trade the CPU audits would reopen. Not taken: 2.7 s/day against a loop that needs its own equivalence proof; reopen if the reviews count per day rises well above 3. 2026-10-29 (run harness-speed-refusal-write-20261029T053222Z-7ac7): reopened, the 2026-10-09 premise that no slot hold belongs to an attended chat no longer holds. review-cells waits journal 93 cell holds, 7676 s in 7 days, 83 of them from the attended chat 77a2b895 (a T2 panel on 10-23, 5 cells 231 s each on 10-28 22:42); across all pools slot_room's reason 'room' held workers 16718 s, review-cells 7676 s, run-suites 1263 s. Cause in share/slots.sh slot_room: it refused room at memory pressure level > 1, i.e. macOS warn, this Mac's resting state with 5-7 GB available (the same veto llm-legs@39e352a8 removed from image-fanout on 2026-10-26). Of the room holds with memlogd cover (10-26..29), none had available MB under the floor; by a rough load1 vs 15-min-mean test about 60 % of the held seconds were the load rule (left as designed: 1155 s of review-cells on 10-28) and the rest, review-cells 672 s, workers 4711 s, run-suites 628 s, were level 2 or a load the rough test missed. Fix: the veto is level >= 4, the available-MB floor and the load rule decide room as before. Remaining wait is reviewer model time. 2026-10-20 (run harness-speed-time-wait-loop-20261020T114213Z-1337): unchanged, the poll still sits at review-bench share/rbench/cli.py PANEL_POLL_S = 2.0, ~1 s a review x ~3 a day. 2026-10-10 (Harness Doctor): not a bug. The wait is reviewer model time, which Speed never trades; its non-model parts are about 1 s of poll per review and the relay is cut (ee185fa8); blind spot delegation-model-time keeps the measure gap. 2026-10-09: ruled out. The slice is attended `review-bench wait` (bin/speed-doctor delegation_leaf), launch to notification. Non-model parts measured: (1) the review-waiter Agent relay, retired in llm-legs@ee185fa8, cost 2.1 s spawn + 1.4 s final message (medians, 109 waiter transcripts in ~/.claude/projects) of a 671 s median wait; 62 of the window's 67 rows predate it; (2) review-bench cmd_wait polls panel_still_running every PANEL_POLL_S 2 s, ~1 s per review; (3) review-cells slot holds (launch.py admitted): all 106 on 2026-10-09 (9892 s, p50 68 s) belong to the unattended bench chat 7977deeb, none to the attended chat c0f23f02. The rest is reviewer cells' model time, which Speed never trades. Cheapest cut: event-driven panel exit instead of the 2 s poll saves ~1000 ms x ~3/day, costs a review-bench change (another repository). The slice lever's 30 % saving is the generic SLICE_LEVER, not a measurement: see blind_spots delegation-model-time.

equivalence.compared: run_streamed's loop before and after: the stall, duration and hold checks run on the same STALL_POLL_S tick, the one change is that a cell's exit wakes the loop at once (a reaper thread sets an Event) instead of after the rest of a time.sleep; the interrupt check keeps its assertion (the group is killed, the descendant dies) and interrupts through Popen.poll
equivalence.data: test_review_bench.sh whole, a time.sleep tally by call site over the whole suite, and 20 runs of /usr/bin/true through run_streamed, load 95-205 on 10 cores, 2026-10-13
equivalence.result: requested sleeps 52.1 s (run_streamed:667 about 51 s) to 0.6 s; an instant cell 106 to 19 ms; PASS before and after, test_review_bench_panels, test_cell_runtime, test_agy_bare and test_consistency PASS; removing the BaseException kill in run_streamed makes the interrupt check fail (descendant survived)

rows.note: 2026-10-13: p10 wall 62 s on 19 s CPU, idle 42 s; the 82 s direct run at load 95 held 31 CPU-s, the rest a run-queue wait that no suite lever owns, plus 52 s of requested time.sleep, 99 % of it run_streamed's 0.25 s poll tick (each fixture cell's exit waited out the rest of a tick; the doctor's PATH-shim profile never sees a Python sleep, so no profiled run bounded it). Fixed: an Event the cell's reaper thread sets; production gains the same ~90 ms per cell exit. Ruled out: the select/communicate waits of the ~980 subprocess.run calls (bin/review-bench and rbench start-up, ~1.2 s wall for 0.15 s CPU at load 95 is the scheduler, not a sleep), the suite's own 0.05 s fixture polls (0.6 s requested). Not done: the stall-fixture sleeps that ARE the premise (hanger.sh, stall_s=1, sleeper.sh at body 1231-1290), the suite's 9.3k-line single process (a split into shards is the long-pole row's lever and the doctor's heavy floor reads the run count). Blind spot: the idle bound reads requested sleeps of shimmed binaries only. 2026-10-14 (night 8004): ruled out again after ceb9b12 held. Direct run at load 20-40: wall 52-54 s, cpu 31-32 s (user 14 + sys 16-17), the other ~21 s the run queue at 57 % CPU, Python time.sleep 3.4 s over the whole suite (cli.py:706 await_panel_run_id 15 x 0.2 s = 3.0 s, subprocess.py poll 0.4 s), the stall fixtures' own bash sleeps (0.3-1.5 s each, the premise of the stall and duration checks), 133+140 bin/review-bench and rbench CLI spawns at 35 ms each. Tried: await_panel_run_id polling 0.01 doubling to 0.2 instead of 0.2 flat, 52.0 s -> 52.4 s wall, so reverted (the marker waits for the child's own start). The journaled 'bounded by the sleeps' reads a vacuous 3670 s: sleep_s sums the requested argument of every shimmed sleep, six of them `sleep 600` fixtures killed in about a second, so min(p10 - floor, median(slept)) is always p10 - floor. Cost of the cheapest cut: sharding the 9.3k-line script saves about 20 s wall x 1 run/day, costs one rbench start-up (~0.7 s CPU) per shard and is the pole row's lever.

rows.title: stop-dispatch killed notice-connections.sh at its 5 s cap (usual 0.1 s): 6 of 9 kills in 24 h, 2026-10-19/20
rows.note: 2026-10-29 regression read: not notice-connections (its last kill 2026-10-20 13:02Z, none in the 9 days since ab0da798). Kills since: notice-word-journal 10-22 22:30Z, 10-24 03:04Z (with notice-chat-names, one batch stall), 10-29 11:29Z alone, each in a swap-bound stretch (system-doctor ticks: busy 0.99-1.0, swap 0.82-0.90, pagein 4-12k/s). word-journal's usual 0.05 s is its jq fast path; its python3 words_journal.py runs only on a turn with a notice, a silent keyword or a ⚡ line, so x101 over usual is the slow path under page-in, not a hang (no hang in its code: the 30 s late wait is already detached). The hook is live (harness-doctor words_journal reads its journal). Ruled out: detaching it like ab0da798 (main reads last.json, turn and last.txt, which the next prompt's intake rewrites, so a detached row could judge the wrong turn). Seen, not cut: main's chat-name subprocess (2 s timeout) sits in the stop; words-log could name the chat at read time. 2026-10-20: 9 kills in 24 h (hits.jsonl), 6 of them notice-connections (6 of its 420 runs; 15 over 2 s, against notice-reports 1 and word-journal 4), 3 siblings only inside two stops where the whole notice batch stalled (2026-10-19 22:48Z; 2026-10-20 10:06Z: chat-names, connections, word-attested killed together, word-journal 4.25 s, usual 0.03-0.12 s). Samples at the kills: busy 0.92-0.997 in 4 of 5; load average 140-272 during this run. The connections check is 0.06-0.1 CPU-s under Homebrew python3 (0.36-0.51 s wall at load 210, no stall reproduced); the read-only path waits on nothing (2026-10-14 note). Fix: with the report bus and a session id the check runs detached and posts its notice to the chat's queue (report-bus post --session), so no stop waits on it or kills it; it was the slowest notice in 229 of 586 stops (+87 s stop wall over 3 days). Not fixed: kills of the other notices in a whole-batch stall (load, the limit's own normal); a recurrence there is that, not this hook (blind spot hook-off-cpu-wait still unattributed). Ruled out: lock contention (no sync since 10-08, last-sync.json), log-sweep I/O (no sweep within 15 min of any kill), memory (mem_free 36-84). Found: /usr/bin/python3 (Xcode 3.9) runs with dont_write_bytecode and no stdlib __pycache__, 0.23 CPU-s for this check against 0.08 under Homebrew's; the killed chats' PATH puts /opt/homebrew/bin first, so not this cause, but any hook reached through /usr/bin/python3 pays it.

rows.title: run-suites outlives the caller's Bash cap: the run continues detached and the next `tests/run-all --attach <run>` call waits on it, so a killed call never reruns the suites
rows.note: 2026-10-30 (run 4436): quiet; not built: goal bash-cap (35d604a3) moves a capped call to the background. 2026-10-30 (run 543f): quiet; not built: goal bash-cap (35d604a3) moves a capped call to the background. 2026-10-29 (run 7550): quiet; not built: goal bash-cap (35d604a3) moves a capped call to the background. 2026-10-29 (run 387d): quiet; not built: goal bash-cap (35d604a3) moves a capped call to the background. 2026-10-20 (run 2c2a): not built: Breakages goal bash-cap (docs/directions/breakages.md) lets a worker's timed-out call move to the background instead, and says this tool is not built. Evidence: ~/.claude/projects transcripts 2026-10-07..14: 64 foreground tests/run-all|run-suites calls ended 'Command timed out after Nm' (41 at timeout=1500000, the claudeb worker cap bin/worker-run:1120), 61 of them followed by another run-all within 15 calls; those 61 killed calls held 1360 min = 8.7 reruns/day x 22.3 min lost each = 194 min/day of worker wall (30 d: 337 timed-out suite calls, 3860 min). Causes vary (slot waits under night load, wide selections, slow suites: RUN_SUITES_SUITE_FLOOR 1800 s is above the 1500 s worker cap, so a suite past 25 min is always killed by Claude Code, never by run-suites' own bound), which is why rows log_audit:worker-suite-run-waits (ruled-out: load), log_audit:foreground-run-all-10min-cap and log_audit:runall-foreground-timeout-cap (fixed by raising the cap) never removed the rerun; this tool removes the lost work whatever the cause. Native route checked: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 (bin/worker-run:1116) stays, -p still drops background shells ~5 s after its result (claude-code issue 65498, CLI 2.1.299 here). Build: share/run-suites.sh starts its run body in its own session (python3 os.setsid, macOS has no setsid(1)) writing the existing per-suite logs and table under a run dir; the foreground waits until BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (exported by worker-run) minus a margin, then prints 'still running: tests/run-all --attach <dir>' and exits with a distinct code, never a FAIL; --attach waits on the same run and prints its table. Reuse the slot hold, owner_watch and journal unchanged. Proof: test_run_suites_timeout-style fixture with a cap shorter than a sleeping suite: the attach prints the suite's PASS and the journal holds one run, not two; Speed reads timed-out-then-rerun calls per 1000 suite runs before against after.

rows.title: bin/wait-until: block until a pid exits, a pgrep pattern clears, a glob reaches N files or a log matches a regex, capped at the Bash cap, so a worker stops polling background jobs with fixed sleeps

equivalence.result: old rule 3.3 min of overshoot (84 calls whose sleep stood outside every loop body = 3.1, 11 real polls = 0.2); new rule 0.2: the outside sleeps read 'sleep N' = end unknown, counted nothing as the design says; the 7 asserts fail on the old wait_call (sleep 100 after a for read 'loop, sleep 100') and pass on the new

rows.note: 2026-10-29 (run harness-speed-time-wrapup-20261029T112133Z-4564, opportunity:time/wait_loop measured, no cut tried, left open): 120 s/day over 58 hand-written poll loops in 24 h, 48 of them inside worker-run runs whose BRIEF_PREAMBLE names wait-until, 10 in chats, median overshoot 1.0 s (half of a sleep 2); three loops (sleep 60/30/20) are 55 s. No Bash-time hint exists; a PreToolUse nudge on sleep loops would buy at most 2 s a call with a rewrite turn a call, the English-gate trap. 2026-10-20: built as designed (bin/wait-until: pid | gone | files | log, 2 s poll, default cap BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS minus 30 s, a pgrep match in the call's own ancestry ignored), named in BRIEF_PREAMBLE by absolute path since a worker's cwd is any sweep repository; no ~/.local/bin link needed. Chats see no hint until a backticked line in a CLAUDE.md names it (tool_mining.facing counts only those): the proposal went to the orchestrator, MD-GUARD. Day totals 2026-10-18..20 still show 2.7 min/day of fixed-sleep waits before the preamble reaches a run. Evidence: ~/.claude/projects transcripts: foreground Bash calls with sleep >= 30 s followed by a status check (ls|wc of an out dir, tail of a log, pgrep/ps): 2026-10-07..14 44.7 wait episodes/day (logo-vectorizer-bench out counts 8.4/day, median last poll 600 s; log/pid waits 36.3/day, median 115 s); the job ends at an unknown point of the last fixed sleep, so each episode overshoots half its last poll: 47.9 + 73.5 = 121 min/day of wall (30 d: 75 episodes/day, 188 min/day; 141 polls/day, 160 sleeps killed at the cap). Sample: the 10 longest worker runs of 30 d (7 logo-vectorizer-bench lanes) spent 1955 min in sleep calls, e.g. 'sleep 1500; ls out/c46-pad | wc -l' timing out at 25 min, and a trace that ended 16:27:07 read at 16:33:43. Root: claudeb workers run with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 (bin/worker-run:1116), so no completion notification exists; rows log_audit:hung-commands-25min-timeout and log_audit:sleep-poll-loops-waiting ruled the sleeps model conduct (no component), which a tool, not a ban, answers. Build: one bin/wait-until (bash, no fork per poll beyond the check; 2 s poll; default max = BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS minus 30 s; prints the condition met or 'timeout after S' and exit 0/1), named once in BRIEF_PREAMBLE's TEST LOOP clause next to the suite wording; grep found no existing wait helper (worker-run wait covers worker runs only). Proof: its suite with a fixture pid/glob/log; Speed counts fixed-sleep poll episodes and their seconds per 1000 Bash calls before against after, net of the preamble bytes. 2026-10-29 (run 7a9f): the 2.6 min/day left after the tool was mostly the doctor's own misreading, not model polling: wait_call took any call holding a for/while anywhere as a poll loop, so `for s in a b; do (job &); done; sleep 100; ls out` read 'loop, sleep 100' and lost 50 s; of 3.3 min of loop-shaped overshoot in 1.2 days 3.1 had the sleep outside every loop body (pixel-forge and logo-vectorizer-bench workers launching jobs, then one sleep). A loop now needs a sleep inside its do..done; passive proof only, the events journal keeps the old shapes of earlier days. Real polls left 0.2 min; chats see no wait-until hint (no CLAUDE.md names it).

rows.title: bin/red-on-old <ref> <file>... -- <cmd>: swap the named files to <ref>, run the covering command, always restore, print red/green for both sides, replacing the hand-made revert/run/restore mutation check
rows.note: 2026-10-30 (run 4436): quiet; block 9 still postponed (docs/directions/README.md:29). 2026-10-30 (run 543f): quiet; block 9 still postponed (docs/directions/README.md). 2026-10-29 (run 7550): quiet; block 9 still postponed (docs/directions/README.md:20). 2026-10-29 (run 387d): quiet; block 9 still postponed (docs/directions/README.md). 2026-10-20 (run 2c2a): not built: block 9 (ad-hoc scripts become tools) is postponed (docs/directions/README.md, Egor 2026-10-20). Evidence: ~/.claude/projects transcripts 2026-10-07..14: 209 in-place swaps of old code (git show REF:P > P with the same path, git checkout REF -- P, git stash) = 29.9 episodes/day, each spanning 6.4 assistant turns until the restore (cp back, stash pop, git checkout HEAD --); one call instead saves 5.4 turns x 4.8 s (median tool_result -> next turn gap over 203k turns of 30 d) = 12.9 min/day (30 d: 11.2 episodes/day, 6.8 turns). The worker preamble prescribes exactly this dance (bin/worker-run BRIEF_PREAMBLE: 'a mutation check is one run of the covering suite (revert -> fails -> restore)') and every P1/P2 fix needs a red-on-old-code test, so the rate follows the night's fix count. A forgotten restore in a shared checkout is the side risk the trap removes. Build: bin/red-on-old in bash: copy the current files to a mktemp dir, git show <ref>:<path> over each, run the command, restore by trap on EXIT/INT/TERM, rerun the command on the restored tree, print 'old: FAIL n / new: PASS n' from the command's exit codes; no git index use (memory rule never stage in the shared index). Name it in BRIEF_PREAMBLE in place of the parenthesised steps. Proof: a fixture repo suite asserting the tree is byte-identical after a killed run; Speed counts in-place swap episodes per 1000 Bash calls before against after.

rows.title: test_store_lock · llm-legs: two racing stale-lock breakers both held the lock, and the winners waited out 120 s
rows.note: Run 41185 (2026-10-13 17:18-17:20, full run, load ~150): 136 s, cpu 22.6 s, rc 1, log 'racing waiters did not settle on a single stale-lock winner'; every racer prints enter or lost, so 136 s means two entered and each waited its 120 s for a third 'lost'. The cause is store_lock_acquire's rename-aside break: a breaker that judged the old lock stale could mv a racer's live newborn aside and put it back only onto a free path, and a newcomer's mkdir in that gap took the lock while the racer still held it (rm -rf of the captured newborn). 6b095a8a breaks under <lock>.break and re-judges the lock in place; the capture case now adds a newcomer mid-break (red on the old code: 'lost its owner to a newcomer: two holders'), the winners stop once all 4 racers resolved, and cleanup kills the sleep 600 owners (a failed assert kept a caller's | tail pipe open 10 min). 5 consecutive runs at load 160 passed; 11 checks.

The listed wrapper commands/<name>.md stays judged as its own root. Checked: no symlink in ~/.claude/skills or any project .claude/skills points into skills-on-demand. Not fixed: a move between two listed roots (skills/a to skills/b) still reads as growth of the new root, since the doctor joins no DELETED+ADDED pair of equal bytes.

rows.note: Python, so it cannot source hook-time.sh; added in 745c775e without a timing line. rows.title: Models edit files with a python string-replace script where the Edit tool does the job
rows.note: 2026-10-29 (fixer 1a49) ruled out: the Edit tool is no faster than the script for this job. 24 h of transcripts to 17:30 UTC: 619 calls (508 by workers), 527 python .replace scripts, 92 sed/perl -i; of the 229 scripts with one .replace( 133 are a def rep()/for-loop helper doing many, 96 a single replace. End to end (gap from the previous tool result to the call, plus its run): an Edit call 3.6 + 0.77 s (2412 calls, 462 chars, 1 % errors), a single-replace script 5.6 + ~0.7 s (3.9 s median with the run it bundles), a partial Read 3.1 + 0.15 s (593 of 671 Edits after a Read follow a partial one, so offset/limit suffices). Edit saves 1.9 s only on a file already Read with nothing run after; 70 % of 1-2-replace targets were never Read, Written or Edited before (a Read first loses 1.3 s), a bundled run needs its own turn (loses ~1.6 s), and from two replaces on Edit is a turn each (2-replace script 8.7 s gap against 2 x 4.4 s). Tried: a once-per-session additionalContext nudge in claude-setup hooks/worker-edit-guard.sh for any session on one .replace( then a write: ~15 eligible calls/day x 1.9 s, about even net, 18 gate-replay rows turning notice; reverted, not landed (its bash 3.2 ${input#*...} took 2.6 s CPU on a 64 KB payload, regexes did not). The predicted 40 min/day prices the scripts' whole writing as removed (blind_spots covered-tool-turns). Found, not this row's: worker-edit-guard records a python write only by its literal path, so p='bin/x'; open(p,'w') reaches no shell-writes record. Earlier: the bypass-mode system prompt prefers sed/heredocs/short scripts; every worker brief's EDITS line already asks for Edit/Write; the graft.py and layers.py corruptions (run 2dc2) were such scripts.

rows.title: Speed's hung lever: a headless claudeb run held open past its final answer by a background shell it left running

equivalence.compared: worker-run-backstop.sh at the night base vs the fix: its stdout per Stop payload
equivalence.data: 955 worker stops of 2026-10-15..29 rebuilt from the stop journal (each row's busy bg-task:N as N running shells), plus continued (stop_hook_active), subagent, malformed and chat payloads
equivalence.result: 935/955 identical (empty), 20 new asks, exactly the stops with live background work; continued, subagent, malformed and chat payloads identical; the worker path 22 -> 35 ms a stop

rows.note: 2026-10-29 (run 3dc7): at 17:41Z the 24 h's hung time is still that one 1800 s idle kill (13.4 h before the fix landed 07:03Z), 0 s in the 10.6 h since (time_budget.budget). 2026-10-29 (run 2a66): the row's 30.0 min/day at 11:30 is still exactly that one 1800 s kill inside its 24 h window (final answer 03:18Z, the fix 06:40Z), none since; it leaves the window 2026-10-30 03:18Z. bin/doctor-fix SPEED_FILES names worker-run-backstop.sh for time/hung, so its packet carries the component. 2026-10-29: the 30 min/day is one idle kill in 14 days (claudeb-1793241723-31255-3e8c): its final answer at 03:18:19Z, then claude -p 2.1.312 waited on the dev server it started with run_in_background (timeout 7200000) until the 1800 s idle watchdog TERMed it, result empty and the run journaled failed with its work committed. The next run of the same brief (claudeb-1793245780-57053-417e) was held 8 min to its server's default background cap, whose notification woke the model and its 'correction' note replaced the report as .result. Native: print mode waits for live background tasks after the last turn; CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS (default 600000) is skipped while a shell has a live deadline (holdForBackgroundShells, off only past a --max-budget-usd), so no env setting ends it. Ruled out: a shorter watchdog trigger on 'answered and held' (18 of 20 live-task worker stops in 14 days were woken legitimately by a task notification up to 569 s later); killing the shells from outside (the kill enqueues a notification that wakes the model and replaces the report). Fix: the backstop asks a worker's stop with live background work once to stop what it no longer needs, wait for the rest and restate its answer.

rows.title: Speed's refusal lever: english-gate denied Russian elsewhere in a worker-run call that hands no text to a model

equivalence.compared: english-gate at the night base vs the fix: exit code, stdout and stderr per Bash call
equivalence.data: 1000 distinct launcher-bearing Bash commands of the last 3 days' transcripts (300 naming worker-run wait/stop/report/transcript/claim/browse/--help, 700 others; seed 5, cwd as recorded), scratch cwd /tmp, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset; plus the 24 denied payloads of the last 8 days rebuilt from transcripts
equivalence.result: 1000/1000 identical (977 allow, 23 deny); the only calls that change are a worker-run segment with a non-text subcommand beside Russian text elsewhere in the command (the 2 denials of session e4ebb028, a `grep` pattern beside `worker-run --help`), pinned in tests/test_english_gates.sh (worker-run wait|report|stop|transcript|claim|browse|--help allowed, say|run|start and a later say still denied)

rows.note: 2026-10-29 (fixer 10d5): the 24 h window's 93 s (the doctor's 1.55 min/day) are 8 denials read off the transcripts: 5 derived-brief ones (a brief written by `sed`, `{ echo ...; cat src; } > brief`, `judge.py brief`; 2.0, 4.7, 12.5, 4.8 and 59.8 s from the denial to the model's next call, 83.8 s), 2 false catches (e4ebb028, a `grep` of Russian words beside `worker-run --help`: 3.8 and 4.5 s) that the landed 64efa12 allows (replayed on both commands, rc 0), 1 true catch (a Russian handoff edit, 2.3 s). The window is a heavy day: the 7-day figure of fixer 225c was 0.38 min/day. Only the derived-brief class is left and it is the gate's design (an unreadable brief cannot be checked; narrowing it is a Never item); cut `read the grouped echo/printf operands of a derived brief` saves ~84 s on this day, ~25 s/day over 7 days (1 denial a day at ~5 s, 225c), costs a parser for sed/cat/printf/echo operand forms in a gate. Ruled out on that price again. 2026-10-29: 19 english-gate denials in 7 days cost 158 s of recovery (0.38 min/day; the doctor's 0.59 is its 24 h window). By kind, read off the transcripts: about 11 true catches (Russian in a memory file, a handoff or a brief, a long Russian quote in `worker-run say`), 2 false catches fixed here, about 6 `brief cannot be read before this call runs` (4 of the last 3 days derive the brief by a redirect from another file or by a program, `sed ... src > brief`, `{ echo; cat src; } > brief`, `judge.py brief`, 2-13 s each; 2 older ones do not reproduce). The derived-brief denial is by design (tests/test_english_gates.sh pins `cat /src > brief` as deny: a brief whose text is not in the command cannot be checked before it exists) and lifting it narrows a deny class, the speed design's Never list; cut `read the derived brief's source operands and judge them` saves about 5 s x 1/day, costs a parser for sed/cat/printf operand forms inside a gate. Ruled out on that price. Older rows of the same message (2ddedf36 10-23, 233cceb1 10-24, heredoc written to a relative path then launched by an absolute one) predate the 10-23/10-25 argv fixes or are a cwd mismatch of the call itself; they replay as allow once the file exists, so they are not reproducible.

rows.note: 2026-10-29 (fixer 10d5): the same cause as speed-hook-commit-report, found with it: rj_live_writes parsed the repository's anchors store with jq on every Edit of a dirty file with a foreign journal entry (llm-legs 0.37 s), now read from rows kept beside the store (rj_anchor_rows). Left: the awk over the writes journal (llm-legs 760 KB) is ~20 ms. 2026-10-29: hook-time rows, 3 whole days: 82-219 of 960-2450 runs a day take over 300 ms and are 1.45-3.31 of the day's 1.5-7.7 hook minutes, p50 78-114 ms. The tail is the dirty-file path: with a foreign owner in the writes journal, same_owner loads run_sessions, a grep -Hx over 3000 worker-session/session files (0.3-1 s, 0.74 s in a bash -x trace of one call), the same cause as hook_grows_repos:edit-conflict-notice.sh (a chat in 5+ repositories meets more foreign rows). Fix: the finished runs' lines are an index beside unswept-runs (same stamp, extended with the directories touched since it, rebuilt whole after a day), only unswept runs are grepped; a worker-session or session file of a finished run is never written after exit_code (0 of 2987). Left: the clean path (git status 12 ms, the written blob's jq and hash-object 14 ms, rj_writes_note's git rev-parse 14 ms, dirname/date/wc forks, 3-5 ms each) is 70-110 ms of which an estimated 15 ms is a plain-checkout fast path for rj_writes_note's rev-parse; not built, it re-derives git's output (dubious-ownership and GIT_DIR cases differ) for about 0.2 min/day. Bash 3.2 `read -d ''` of a 360 KB file takes 1.1 s, which is why the index is grepped from its file and never read into a variable.

rows.title: claudeb broke 7 account-store locks by age (41-91 s) in 24 h, holders possibly alive
rows.note: All 7 breaks (2026-10-28 18:07Z-10-29 02:55Z, com/notcom/locomthebest .json.lock) sit in swap-bound stretches: system ticks busy 1.0, swap 86-93 %, pagein 1500-7700/s, 60 s ticks taking 67-478 s; no claudeb or llm-refresh change since 10-20. The lock's premise (no live writer holds 30 s) fails on such a machine, and an age break let a second writer race the holder (lost merge; on the rlock/glock a double POST of a single-use refresh token). Fix: claudeb's lock_acquire/lock_release and oauth_attempt_update's own loop use share/store-lock.sh's pid-owned lock, which never breaks a live holder before its 3600 s ceiling and breaks a dead one at once; the rlock re-touch loop and the 10 s token-spacing clamp, both there only for the 30 s age break, are gone. claudeb.lock-stale and claudeb.lock-retries leave limits.json (store-lock.retries/ceiling/ownerless-stale journal instead). test_claudeb's live-holder case is red on the old code (breaks a 120 s lock of a live pid, never takes a dead pid's). Load itself is weather (logo-vectorizer-bench, JumpConnect, a hidden Chrome).

rows.title: instruction watcher's repo listing killed at 20 s 38 times in 24 h (2026-10-29 01:30-02:35Z)
rows.note: Every 120 s tick's repo task scan died at 20 s from 01:30Z to 02:35Z, the night's worst stall (60 s system ticks took 69-478 s, busy 1.0, swap 0.87-0.92, pagein 2000-4000/s; restore-all.sh's hidden Chrome, JumpConnect and the bench on top). The 20 s cap exists because a synchronous scan blocks Hammerspoon's main thread; the listing has run as an hs.task since llm-legs@ae761633b and W.busy keeps ticks from overlapping, so killing it bought nothing and threw away each scan's work. Fix: task scans get TASK_LIMIT_S = WATCH_TICK - 10 (110 s, own limit instruction-watch.task-timeout); synchronous ones keep 20 s. rows.title: Speed's refusal lever: commit-push-gate refused a commit in a free repository behind a cd, because a || after every git made the cd untrusted

equivalence.compared: the gate's verdict on the same commands before and after: rf_git_dirs sets `branchy` (a cd then no longer counts as entered) from the command text up to its last git instead of the whole text
equivalence.data: RF_THROWAWAY_ROOTS=/nonexistent hook runs from a gated cwd: `cd FREE && git commit -m msg; P=$(lsof -t); [ -n "$P" ] && echo $P || echo free` old exit 2, new 0; `cd FREE || echo no; git commit -m msg` old 2, new 2; `cd FREE && git commit -m msg` old 0, new 0; two asserts added to tests/test_review_flow_gate.sh beside the cd-into-free-repository cases
equivalence.result: a branch operator before the last git still keeps the cd untrusted (the cd may not have run); one after it cannot change where an earlier git landed, so a commit in a repository that wires no door is no longer refused for the session cwd's door

rows.note: 2026-10-29: of the 3 refusals in the 24 h window (29.7 s recovery, 0.5 min/day) two are the door working: 07:37Z a commit in rentalhub-docs without a word, and the retry whose WORD= quote was shortened with an ellipsis, 'WORD= was not found in his last message' (11 s); the third, 03:49Z, was a false catch: the chat's cd into Rentiva-design (a free repository, origin /Volumes/Work/Sites/Rentiva) then git add/commit, followed by `P=$(lsof ...); ... || echo` in the same call, was refused as rentalhub-wired because commit-push-gate.sh rf_git_dirs set `branchy` from any || or & in the whole command, so the cd was not trusted and the commit fell back to the session cwd (Rentiva, wired). Its recovery span was ~1 s (the next call ran at once) but the commit was never redone in that minute. Fixed in claude-setup. rows.title: context-nudge slower in transcripts over 10 MB
rows.note: Its own work, not load: 24 h CPU p50 38 ms under 1 MB, 54 over 10 MB (x1.42) while hooks of the same batches stay x0.9-1.17. Not history: at equal growth a 24 MB and a 0.4 MB transcript cost the same. Bytes a call brings: big transcripts are image-heavy, tool_result p90 400 KB against 15 KB, and the hook paid them twice, bash `read -d ''` takes the payload pipe one byte a syscall (0.4 ms CPU a KiB: 22 ms at 1 KiB, 218 at 500 KiB) and macOS tail -c +N copies the sidecar's new bytes at ~31 MB/s. jq now reads stdin itself and dd seeks to the block, as llm-legs statusline.sh does since 6baaa4e1: 60 sampled real tool responses of today's big transcripts, mean CPU 49 -> 23 ms a run, small ones 23 -> 23; a 500 KiB payload 228 -> 25 ms. Same output: the same four fields reach the same checks; dd starts at most one block before the old start, and earlier boundaries only re-find what the sorted maximum holds. Ruled out: the sweep (daily) and the boundary jq (only on a compact_boundary in the new bytes). Found on the way and fixed (claude-setup@ecc8c7d): a transcript smaller than the sidecar's scanned offset (a rewrite) was skipped until it outgrew it, keeping the old file's boundary; it now resets and rescans, statusline.sh's rule; test_context_nudge red on 204640e. rows.title: memlogd's 1 GB frames cap evicted 3-day-old incident frames as memory-pressure episodes rose to 11 a day
rows.note: 2026-10-30: unchanged, 43 drops in 24 h of frames 48-54 h old (10-27T18:22 .. 10-28T02:30) as INCIDENT lines ran 8, 15, 6 on 10-28..30; frames/ holds 1.0 G. The cap did its job: evict_frames dropped the oldest frames (10-26T16:34-18:32, 35-88 MB each) for newer episodes, a day before rotate_files' 3-day retention would delete them anyway; INCIDENT lines (5, 1, 8, 11 on 10-26..29, avail under 4 GB) stay in the day logs. rows.title: store-lock broke claudeb account-store locks a killed statusline render left without a pid (6 in 24 h, 89-121 s old)
rows.note: Creator found: bin/statusline.sh takes the same <account>.json.lock (snapshot_lock_acquire, a bare mkdir with no pid) around its rate-limit cache merge, and Claude Code aborts a running render on every new trigger (2.1.314: the status line controller's #b() calls abort() on the previous render), so a render killed inside the merge (a jq that a swap-bound machine stalls for seconds) left a pid-less directory; the statusline itself reclaims it only after 120 s, and claudeb's store-lock breaks it as ownerless past 30 s, which is the 89-121 s ages of the 6 breaks on 10-29 (and claudeb.lock-stale's 7 before llm-legs@bfb86732, all at swap 86-93 %). The previous note's 'only claudeb writes these locks' was wrong. Fix: an EXIT trap guarded by rl_lock_held removes the lock when the render dies by SIGTERM/SIGHUP (fixture render, jq stalled under the lock, SIGTERM: lock left on HEAD, released after). Not covered: a SIGKILL, whose orphan still breaks as before; the abort's signal was not confirmed in the bundle.

rows.title: run-suites runs a `# shards:` suite whole when slot_room fails at the run's start, and the run then waits the whole suite as its long pole
rows.note: 2026-10-30 dig redo (lens: work done serially that could run at once). share/run-suites.sh shards a suite only while suite_shard_wanted's slot_room finds room (`wait` suites aside), so a run started in a load spike runs it as one job. Critical path: ~/.cache/run-suites/runs.jsonl 10-16..29 (865 runs, raw_decode), per run the slowest suite's secs less the runner-up's when the slowest is a suite journaled sharded elsewhere (45 suites) but here without `shards`: 9.9 runs/day, 28.7 waited min/day (test_doctor_fix 9.45, test_review_flow_gate 3.86, test_night_run 3.68, test_night_carry 3.54, test_statusline_hooks 2.05); whole runs read wall/CPU 2.3-4.2 against 0.5-1.07 sharded (test_doctor_fix median 312 s whole, 90 s sharded, CPU 117/115 s). The cause is load, not memory: all 69 such poles 10-27..30 started at 4,240-10,036 MB available (memlogd day logs), over chat-load's 2,048 MB guard plus a slot's need. Estimate: per run min(excess over the runner-up, wall x (1 - sharded/whole)): 20.4 min/day at a ratio of 0.5, 11.7 at 0.75, 5.0 at 0.9. Proof, fixed now: First step, test_doctor_fix on one tree, RUN_SUITES_SHARDS=on against off, three interleaved pairs while slot_room prints a `load` reason; sharded/whole over 0.9 stops it. Then the same runs.jsonl measure over the 7 days after landing: shardable whole-pole excess 28.7 -> 0 by memory-free room, waited pole excess of those runs <= 8.3 min/day; memlogd available MB during sharded spike runs never under the guard; PASS counts equal.

rows.title: run-suites runs at most -j cores/2 (5) jobs whatever the room, so a run of more jobs alone on the machine queues them at a median 2.2 cores used
rows.note: 2026-10-30 dig redo (lens: work done serially that could run at once). share/run-suites.sh sets jobs=$(slots_from_cores 2 2) with no room arm, while the run slots themselves are F-M by slot_room. Critical path: ~/.cache/run-suites/runs.jsonl 10-16..29 (865 runs), a run's wall (ended_at - started_at) less its slowest suite's secs: 91.4 min/day, 87.0 of it in the 33.6 runs/day holding more jobs (suites x shards) than j=5; those runs use median 2.16 cores (sum cpu_s / wall, p90 3.35), so their jobs wait on processes and sleeps, not cores. Estimate: list-scheduling replay of each such run's jobs longest first (a shard taken at its suite's journaled max wall; the replay at 5 reads 0.87 of the real wall), new wall = max(slowest suite, sum cpu_s / 10 cores, wall x sim(J)/sim(5)): runs no other run-suites run overlapped (18.2/day) 19.9 min/day at -j 8, 25.5 at -j 10; with overlapped runs 47.7 at -j 8, an upper bound. Proof, fixed now: First step, one recorded >5-job named set (the 12-suite aa474225 of 10-30, llm-legs) on one tree, -j 5 against -j 8, three interleaved pairs while slot_room finds room; -j 8 saving under 17 s a run (5 min/day at 18.2 runs/day) stops it. Then, over the 7 days after landing, the wall beyond the slowest suite of >5-job runs no other run overlapped, per run, against 10-16..29's at equal job counts: lower by the First step's per-run saving, >= 5 waited min/day; memlogd available MB during raised runs never under the guard; run-suites queue (29.7 min/day) no higher.
